text: Then all Israel gathered to David at Hebron and said, "Look, we are your own flesh and blood.

Even in the past, while Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them home. And the LORD your God said to you, 'You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be ruler over my people Israel.'"

So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD. Then they anointed David king over Israel, as the LORD had spoken through Samuel.
David and all Israel marched to Jerusalem, that is, Jebus, where the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were living.
The people of Jebus said to David, "You will never get in here." But David captured the stronghold of Zion, that is, the City of David.
David had said, "Whoever strikes down a Jebusite first shall become chief and commander." Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and so he became chief.
David took up residence in the stronghold; that is why it was called the City of David.
He built up the city all around, from the Millo to the surrounding wall, and Joab restored the rest of the city.
And David grew greater and greater, for the LORD of hosts was with him.
These are the chiefs of David's mighty men, who together with all Israel gave his kingship strong support to make him king, as the LORD had promised concerning Israel.
This is the list of David's mighty men: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the officers. He wielded his spear against three hundred men, killing them in a single encounter.

versions.text: This is the roll of David's mighty men: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the officers. He wielded his spear against three hundred men, killing them in a single encounter.
versions.explanation: "roll" is archaic and can be misheard when read aloud; "list" renders מִסְפַּר naturally and clearly.

text: Next to him was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men.
He was with David at Pas Dammim when the Philistines gathered there for battle. There was a plot of ground full of barley, and the troops fled before the Philistines.
But they took their stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck the Philistines down; and the LORD brought about a great victory.
Three of the thirty chiefs went down to David at the rock, to the cave of Adullam, while a Philistine army was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
At that time David was in the stronghold, and a Philistine garrison was at Bethlehem.
David was seized with longing and said, "If only someone would give me a drink of water from the well by the gate of Bethlehem!"
So the three broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well by the gate of Bethlehem, and carried it back to David. But David refused to drink it; instead he poured it out to the LORD.

"God forbid that I should do such a thing!" he said. "Shall I drink the blood of these men who went at the risk of their lives? For they brought it at the risk of their lives." And he would not drink it. Such were the deeds of the three mighty men.
Abishai the brother of Joab was chief of the three. He wielded his spear against three hundred men and killed them, and he won a name alongside the three.
Of the second group of three he was the most honored, and he became their commander, though he never equaled the first three.

versions.text: He was doubly honored above the three and became their commander, though he was not counted among the three themselves.
versions.explanation: As it stands, "doubly honored above the three" and "not counted among the three" read as a contradiction for a listener. The Hebrew distinguishes ranks; making the two groups explicit removes the apparent self-contradiction and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a valiant fighter from Kabzeel, a man of many exploits. He struck down the two mightiest warriors of Moab, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.

He also struck down an Egyptian, a man about seven and a half feet tall. The Egyptian had a spear like a weaver's beam in his hand, but Benaiah went against him with a club. He wrenched the spear out of the Egyptian's hand and killed him with that very spear.

versions.text: He also struck down an Egyptian, a man seven and a half feet tall. The Egyptian had a spear like a weaver's beam in his hand, but Benaiah went against him with a club. He wrenched the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.
versions.explanation: "his own spear" is ambiguous in English (it could be read as Benaiah's spear), whereas the Hebrew clearly means the Egyptian's spear. Also, since the Hebrew reads "five cubits," the conversion is best softened to "about seven and a half feet" (a footnote noting "Hebrew: five cubits" would be helpful).

text: Such were the deeds of Benaiah son of Jehoiada; he too won a name alongside the three mighty men.
He was held in greater honor than any of the thirty, but he was not counted among the three. And David put him in charge of his bodyguard.
The mighty warriors were: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,
Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,
Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa, Abiezer from Anathoth,
Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,
Maharai the Netophathite, Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite,
Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjaminites, Benaiah the Pirathonite,
Hurai from the ravines of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,
Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,
the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite,
Ahiam son of Sachar the Hararite, Eliphal son of Ur,
Hepher the Mekerathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,
Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai son of Ezbai,
Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar son of Hagri,
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite, Zabad son of Ahlai,
Adina son of Shiza the Reubenite, chief of the Reubenites, and thirty with him,
Hanan son of Maacah, Joshaphat the Mithnite,
Uzziah the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,

versions.text: Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew name עֻזִּיָּא is commonly rendered "Uzzia" or "Uzziah" in English; for oral reading consistency with the familiar form, "Uzziah" is clearer. Either is defensible, so this is a minor stylistic point.

text: Jediael son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite,

versions.text: Jediael son of Shimri, his brother Joha the Tizite,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew word order places "Joha his brother" together, and the appositive "the Tizite" reads more naturally after the name; this also matches the pattern of the surrounding list for smoother oral reading.

text: Eliel the Mahavite, Jeribai and Joshaviah the sons of Elnaam, Ithmah the Moabite,
Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.
